title: Hosting Concierge — Decision Journal for POC Architecture
content:
Decision journal for a mid-sized regulated customer POC evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (and hybrid blends). Purpose: capture rationale, assumptions, tradeoffs, small-run rollout plan, and a minimal runbook that the SE + Eng teams can iterate on during the engagement.

1) One-line summary
Customer wants low-latency search and redaction in-app, with strict data residency for PII. Recommendation: start with Hosted (fast time-to-value) for feature validation + canary traffic; maintain a parallel Dedicated staging pool for latency-critical paths and short-term capacity guarantees; transition to Private/VPC for full production once compliance controls and KMS integrations validated.

2) Customer context (notes from kickoff)
- Vertical: fintech / lending (US + EU customers).
- Data sensitivity: PII, transaction IDs, and KYC documents.
- Traffic profile: peak 1.2k RPS, average 300 RPS. Bursts during market open windows.
- Target p99 latency: <= 120ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Budget: constrained for first 6 months; willing to commit to reserved capacity if SLA improvements measurable.

3) Constraints and non-negotiables
- Data residency: EU customer data must not leave eu-central region.
- Key management: must use customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) for embeddings storage.
- Audit: detailed request logs for 6 months (obfuscation allowed for prompt content).
- SLO: 99.9% availability for core inference endpoints.

4) Options considered (brief)
- Hosted-only: fastest to ship, built-in analytics + model catalog. Downsides: reliance on hosted region presence, harder to meet on-prem KMS SLA and strict egress rules.
- Dedicated-only: reserved GPU pools in customer-chosen region. Predictable latency and throughput, better isolation, can integrate with customer network via peering. Downsides: commit costs, longer lead time to provision.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control, KMS/HSM, easiest path to satisfy strong compliance. Downsides: longer setup, ops burden on customer or professional services.
- Hybrid sequencing: Hosted -> Dedicated staging -> Private production. Allows incremental validation and measured cost ramp.

5) Assumptions & cost model inputs (for tradeoff calc)
- Model: open-llama-70b quantized profile (throughput and memory numbers taken from model catalog).
- Token mix: 80% short completion (<= 64 tokens), 20% long (>= 256 tokens).
- Batching efficiency: hosted auto-batching gives ~1.8x effective throughput; dedicated pooling tuned can reach ~2.6x with smaller latency impact.
- GPU options: A100-80GB equivalent for Dedicated; on-prem may be T4/NVLX depending on customer.
- Ballpark monthly cost (est): Hosted: $X per active hour (low commit), Dedicated reserved: baseline $Y/month for 8-card pool, Private on-prem: CAPEX+ops (one-time + monthly ops).

6) Routing and graceful degradation patterns (proposal)
- Primary: route latency-sensitive traffic (search endpoints) to Dedicated pool in eu-central.
- Secondary: route exploratory / long-tail requests to Hosted.
- Fallback: if Dedicated capacity saturated, fallthrough to Hosted model variant (smaller quantized model) with a tagging header so app can show degraded latency/quality message.
- Canary: 5% traffic to Dedicated from day 1 of staging, then ramp to 50% after SLA verification.

7) Security & compliance integration checklist (minimal for POC)
- Validate VPC peering and IP allowlist with infra team.
- Confirm KMS integration flow: hosted KMS token exchange design + audit of logs.
- Data retention policy: ensure request logs are scrubbed of PII for dev telemetry; full logs delivered to customer S3 with encryption.
- Pen test schedule: 4-week window prior to production cutover.

8) Operational playbook (seed for SE runbook)
- Monitoring: wire per-route latency dashboards; compare p50/p90/p99 across Hosted vs Dedicated.
- Alerting: alert if Dedicated p99 > 120ms for 10 consecutive minutes OR if Dedicated free GPU capacity < 20%.
- Incident: if Dedicated unavailable, auto-reroute to Hosted; SE to notify customer success and open SE-INC for postmortem.
- Cost control: cap burst traffic to Hosted with rate-limits and quota policy to avoid runaway charges.

9) Migration path & timeline (12 week POC -> production lane)
- Week 0–2: Hosted integration, sample prompts, baseline metrics.
- Week 3–4: Dedicated staging pool provisioned; run parallel tests and latency baselining.
- Week 5–8: Security integration (KMS, VPC peering), compliance evidence collection.
- Week 9–12: Traffic ramp to Dedicated; run simulated failover to Hosted; final cutover decision for Private deployment (if required) and timeline estimate.

10) Quality / regression checks to wire in early
- Define 100 prompt-based checks (short/long) from customer domain: track semantics + Hallucination delta between hosted and dedicated quantized variants.
- Automate synthetic load tests that mimic peak burst patterns.

11) Risks and mitigation (bullet list)
- Provisioning delay for Dedicated GPUs -> mitigation: reserve temporary cloud pool for test workloads and push production readiness timeline later.
- KMS integration complexity -> mitigation: early proof-of-concept key exchange with security team, fallback to hosted ephemeral encryption until validated.
- Cost overruns on Hosted during bursts -> mitigation: strict rate limits, per-route quotas, and pre-approved spending thresholds.

12) Open questions (to surface to sales/legal/infra)
- Does customer require complete data plane isolation (no cross-tenant racks) or logical isolation acceptable?
- Are there any export-control requirements for model binaries? (affects private on-prem options)
- Can the customer accept anonymized telemetry for SE debugging for first 30 days?

13) Action items (owner -> due)
- Ava: prepare Dedicated capacity estimate + pricing sketch (due 2024-11-25).
- Jordan: schedule VPC peering runbook review with infra (due 2024-11-21).
- Marcus: seed 50 prompt regression check set and baseline results (due 2024-11-28).

Appendix (fragile / rough notes)
- Example routing header: X-Redwood-Route: dedicated-eu-central; X-Redwood-Fallback: hosted-small-variant
- Quick config snippet (pseudocode):
  routeRules: [
    {match: "/search", prefer: "dedicated-eu", fallback: "hosted-small", quota: 5000/min},
    {match: "/bulk-embed", prefer: "hosted", quota: 200/min}
  ]
